problem.label: The Gap
problem.headline: Many Data Sources. No Architecture to Connect Them.
problem.p1: Most clubs sit on more performance data than ever before. The problem is not volume. It is that the data lives in disconnected systems with no individual model underneath it. No standardised infrastructure. No consolidation strategy. No security architecture built for clinical data. Twinspire is the structured layer that connects what is already being collected.
problem.block3Title: Why Both Streams Are Required by Science
problem.p2: The data your players generate off the training pitch, rest-day recovery scores, sleep quality, nocturnal HRV, never reaches anyone who could act on it. Research is clear: clubs not measuring recovery are not measuring half their performance picture. Training load data alone cannot produce a meaningful readiness observation.
problem.p3: Combining recovery monitoring with training load provides the basis for modelling the athlete as a dynamic system. A 2025 joint modelling study found integrating sleep, HRV, and load data was necessary for robust individual readiness assessment. Without both, you are not modelling a person. You are modelling a session.
problem.originHeading: The Data Existed. The Context Didn't.
problem.originBody: Twinspire began as control engineering research at DTU, applying digital twin methodology to physiological systems. The same principles used to model complex industrial systems for predictive maintenance, building an individual dynamic model, detecting deviation from baseline, surfacing it before failure, were applied to the athlete. The research became a product when Pouya recognised that the gap between what the data showed and what the clinical team knew was not a communication problem. It was an infrastructure problem. Twinspire is the end-to-end data strategy that closes it, built to EU MDR Class IIa standards, with security and data provenance as the foundation rather than a feature layer.

product.p1: When your doctor runs blood tests, they track your values over time because your normal may differ from the reference range. Twinspire does the same for every athlete in your squad, across both the data the club controls and the data the player privately generates.

card1.title: Not a squad benchmark
card1.body: A shift that looks unremarkable across a squad can be a significant warning for a particular player. Each individual's reference behavior is built and measured separately.

card2.title: Trained staff leave. The model does not.
card2.body: A good physio intuitively knows their long-term players. When staff turn over, that knowledge leaves. Twinspire makes it objective, permanent, and transferable.

card3.title: The Athletic Passport
card3.body: Every session, load, injury, and rehab milestone, portable, owned by the athlete. When they transfer, their full history transfers. New club inherits objective data from day one.

product.p2: Players connect their personal wearables and complete a morning check-in directly in the Twinspire app. This is how the private data stream enters the model. The daily check-in captures subjective readiness, sleep quality, and wellness markers that no wearable measures automatically. Both streams together build the individual picture. If your club already has a player-facing app, Twinspire can integrate with it rather than sit alongside it.

faq.title: Frequently Asked
faq.subtitle: The questions clubs, athletes, and partners ask most often.

whatIsTwinspire.question: What is Twinspire?
whatIsTwinspire.answer: Twinspire connects the data your club platform captures with the personal wearable data your players generate off-site, and builds a continuously updated individual baseline for each athlete. The output feeds back into your existing setup as readiness scores, deviation alerts, and trend data. It is a decision support tool for coaching and medical staff, not a replacement for clinical judgment.

whatProblemDoesTwinspireSolve.question: What problem does Twinspire solve?
whatProblemDoesTwinspireSolve.answer: Your club sees GPS and gym load. Your players privately measure wearable recovery, sleep, and HRV at 6am on a Sunday. These two streams have never been properly connected, and that gap is where the early warning signals live. Twinspire bridges them under a proper GDPR and consent framework, builds an individual baseline for each athlete, and surfaces deviation before it becomes injury.

whoIsTwinspireFor.question: Who is Twinspire for?
whoIsTwinspireFor.answer: Twinspire is built for three groups who work together: physiotherapists who need unified deviation alerts across both club and personal data; coaches and performance staff who need true individual readiness before every session; and footballers themselves, who finally have a portable physiological record that belongs to them across their entire career.

howDoesTwinspireWork.question: How does it actually work?
howDoesTwinspireWork.answer: Club data arrives via API, no platform switch required. Player data arrives via the Twinspire app, through a one-time consent setup. Both streams feed the individual baseline model. Twinspire learns what normal looks like for each specific player, then continuously monitors for meaningful deviation. The output, readiness scores, deviation alerts, key drivers, appears in your existing setup.

whatIsAthleticPassport.question: What is the Athletic Passport?
whatIsAthleticPassport.answer: Every time a player transfers, their physiological history resets to zero. A new club inherits a name and a transfer fee, not 18 months of individual baseline data. The Athletic Passport changes that. It is a portable, consent-based record of everything a player's body has generated: sessions, loads, injuries, rehab milestones, and the individual baseline built from both club and personal data. It belongs to the athlete. When they sign for a new club, their baseline arrives with them.

isTwinspireDashboard.question: Is this just another dashboard?
isTwinspireDashboard.answer: No. A dashboard displays variables. It does not explain what matters, why it matters, or what to do next. Twinspire is a decision support system. It builds an individual baseline model for each athlete, monitors continuously across both club and personal data streams, and surfaces deviation with the specific drivers behind it. The output is a decision with visible reasoning, not a score to interpret.

whatIsDigitalTwin.question: What does individual baseline modeling mean in practice?
whatIsDigitalTwin.answer: When your doctor runs blood tests, they track your values over time, because your normal may be different from the population reference range. Twinspire does exactly that for every performance and recovery metric in your squad. It builds what normal looks like for each specific player, across both the data the club controls and the data the player privately generates, and measures everything against it. A shift that looks unremarkable squad-wide can be a significant warning for a particular player.

whatDataDoesTwinspireUse.question: What data does Twinspire use?
whatDataDoesTwinspireUse.answer: From the club side: GPS and movement data, strength and gym output, physio notes and clinical assessments. From the player's own devices: personal wearables including recovery trackers, sleep monitors, and GPS watches, the wearables capturing recovery, sleep, and HRV data off-site that your club platform currently has no access to. Both streams are processed under a proper consent and GDPR framework.

whoOwnsData.question: Who owns the player data?
whoOwnsData.answer: The player owns their Athletic Passport, the longitudinal record of their individual baseline built from both club and personal data. The club owns its squad analytics. Twinspire hosts both under a formal Data Processing Agreement. Player data is never sold, never shared with third parties, and fully portable when a player transfers.

isTwinspireGdprCompliant.question: Is Twinspire GDPR compliant?
isTwinspireGdprCompliant.answer: Yes, and built to a higher standard than most sports platforms. Twinspire is designed with medical device regulation principles, full GDPR compliance, EU-based hosting, and formal Data Processing Agreements for all club integrations. Granular consent controls mean the player decides what they share and can withdraw at any time. This is a structural differentiator as player associations and club legal teams increasingly scrutinise health data handling.

whereIsTwinspireBased.question: Where is Twinspire based and who built it?
whereIsTwinspireBased.answer: Founded at the Technical University of Denmark (DTU) in Copenhagen. Twinspire was started by Pouya Tobias Strand Nikoui, a former professional footballer who suffered a reinjury after full clinical clearance, and returned to DTU to build what the sport was missing. The team combines expertise in AI, individual baseline modeling, platform architecture, and data security. Backed by DTU Skylab and DIF Innovation Lab.

dataEthics.heading: The Compliance Architecture
dataEthics.subtitle: Most sports platforms were built for performance, then had compliance retrofitted. Twinspire started from the other direction.
dataEthics.description: As player unions and club legal teams scrutinise how health data is handled, the compliance architecture your platform is built on matters.
dataEthics.card1: KPIs grounded in physiology, not vanity metrics. Every variable in the model has a validated biological rationale and a defined relationship to athlete readiness.
dataEthics.card2: Technology validated before it reaches a clinical decision. We apply the same validation rigour to our models that medical device standards require before a tool can inform care.
dataEthics.card3: Granular, athlete-owned, withdrawable at any time. The player decides what they share, with whom, and for how long. Consent is not a checkbox on a terms page.
dataEthics.card4: Standardised ingestion across club and personal streams. Every data source enters through the same validated pipeline, ensuring consistency, auditability, and traceability.
dataEthics.disclaimer: Twinspire is a decision support platform. It is not intended to diagnose or treat medical conditions.
dataEthics.card5: Evidence-based, not a black box. Every output surfaces the signals behind it. Staff see what is driving a deviation, not just that one exists.
dataEthics.checklistIntro: Criteria proposed by independent researchers at ECSS Lausanne 2026 for what a genuine individual athlete model requires. Below is where Twinspire stands.

digitalTwin.sectionLabel: What a Decision Support System Actually Is
digitalTwin.heading: A dashboard displays variables
digitalTwin.headingAccent: It does not explain what matters, why it matters, or what to do next
digitalTwin.intro: At ECSS 2026, independent researchers proposed a checklist for what a genuine individual athlete model requires. Below is where Twinspire stands, honestly.

individualized.label: Individualized
individualized.body: Every metric measured against that player's own evolving baseline, not a squad average, not a population norm.

dynamicallyUpdated.label: Dynamically Updated
dynamicallyUpdated.body: The model updates continuously with every new data point from both streams. The longer it runs, the more precisely it understands each player.

connectedToDecisions.label: Connected to Decisions
connectedToDecisions.body: Output is framed as a decision, is this player ready today, not as a data export or a chart to interpret.

explicitAboutUncertainty.label: Explicit About Uncertainty
explicitAboutUncertainty.body: Key drivers surfaced explicitly. Staff see which signals are driving any deviation, not just that a deviation exists.

validatedAgainstOutcomes.label: Validated Against Outcomes
validatedAgainstOutcomes.body: The specific gap the validation cohort is designed to close. We are honest about the fact that it is not yet fully met.

digitalTwin.closingNote: This checklist did not originate with us. We think it should be the industry standard. We are building to it.

intro.p1: At Twinspire, we're developing a digital twin platform for individualised athlete modelling in elite football. Our work sits at the intersection of sports science, data, and performance environments where outcomes matter. Decisions are made under uncertainty, often with incomplete information. That's the context we build for.
intro.p2: We are a small team with a broad range of experience, from early 20s to mid-60s. What unites us is a shared approach: we take ownership, we focus on execution, and we prefer clarity over complexity. There is little interest here in unnecessary process or work that doesn't translate into something tangible.
intro.p3: There is often a perceived trade-off between experience and willingness to build. We do not think that holds. Some people naturally stay close to the work, regardless of seniority. Those are the people we value: individuals who take responsibility, contribute directly, and care about what they produce.
intro.p4: We work out of DTU in Copenhagen, with the flexibility to work from home. We operate with a high level of trust and expect people to manage their time accordingly. We are an international and diverse team, and we see that as a strength.
intro.p5: What you can expect is meaningful ownership, a direct connection between your work and its impact, and an environment where things move without unnecessary friction. We are early, and we are ambitious, which practically means that you'll have the opportunity to shape both the product and how it is being built.
intro.p6: If this sounds like the kind of place you want to contribute, we'd like to hear from you. If you don't see an opening that fits you, reach out regardless. We are growing.
